title: `ward setup`: explicit creation of the vault key and encrypted vault
description: Split out of WCLI-5 on 2026-09-28. T01 and T02 need the encrypted store, and the store is WCLI-6, which comes after the key provider (orchestrator ordering: WCLI-5, then WCLI-6). Spec §6.4 and §8: ward setup runs in a trusted terminal, generates the vault key, stores it through the WCLI-5 KeyProvider, and creates the encrypted vault in ~/.ward (0700 directory, 0600 files). Nothing else ever creates or regenerates a key. An existing database with a missing key is a recovery condition, not a new installation. A crash during setup must never delete existing data or replace an existing key.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T01: setup creates a native keystore item and encrypted state; --help, status and instructions never initialize a store
T02: existing vault with missing, locked or unavailable key fails closed and leaves the vault unchanged
A setup interrupted at any step leaves no replaced key and no deleted or half-written vault, and a rerun either completes or reports a recovery condition

A noninteractive command against a missing, locked or unavailable key fails within a stated bounded time and never waits on a hidden approval prompt, including when a native credential-store call is still pending: the command exits explicitly rather than waiting for the event loop to drain (moved from WCLI-5 on 2026-09-28)

implementationNotes: From the WCLI-5 review (PR #15): (1) KeyProvider.create is check-then-write and not atomic in the store. Setup must serialize Ward against itself, for example with an exclusive lock file in ~/.ward, before creating a key. (2) create can reject with vault_key_write_unconfirmed when the write may have landed. Setup resolves that with load() and never writes again. (3) The KeyProvider bound covers the promise only. A pending napi call can keep the process alive, so setup and every key-using command must exit explicitly after vault_key_unavailable. (4) Do not zero a key buffer on a timed-out write path: the pending native write may still read it.

Tooling finding (2026-09-28): the opum-workflow reviewer specialist refused dispatch on this task: it is gated on a lore review context pack whose profile is .lore/agents/review.toml, and this repository has never had any lore agent profiles (lore agent list: none; git history has no .lore/agents/). A general-purpose agent was dispatched instead to satisfy spec §15's independent-review requirement for this PR. Two things for the owning tools: (1) opum-workflow's reviewer definition now hard-requires a profile this repo was never provisioned with — either the repo needs a profile provisioning step or the reviewer needs a documented fallback; (2) lore agent context review on a missing profile exits 0 with a warning, where the reviewer's protocol documents exit 3 — a dispatcher could read exit 0 as a clean pack. Routed to the orchestrator for lore-cli/opum-fleet.
finalSummary: WCLI-20: ward setup — the one command that ever creates a vault key or a vault. What changed: an application-layer setup flow (injected session/provider/store) with a crash-resume model (a durable setup.json journal pins the vault id before the key write; a rerun at any point completes the same setup or reports a recovery condition, and never replaces a key or deletes a vault); a setup lock that is flock(2)-arbitrated through bun:ffi on macOS with an O_EXCL pid fallback off macOS; write-unconfirmed resolution by load() only, never by writing again; an explicit-exit contract (exitExplicitly on vault_key_unavailable and vault_key_write_unconfirmed, and on success after any abandoned bounded call, with synchronous output writes); the initial vault document {"formatVersion":1}; two setup error codes; async runWard with injected wardDirectory/keyProvider (no env override shipped); an ADR 0001 consequence including the deleted-vault resume limit. Why: spec §6.4 and §8, the task's four criteria, and the four WCLI-5 review obligations. Verified: 240 tests passing locally (bun 1.3.14) and on CI run 36479948490 (self-hosted Linux ARM64, which exercises the fallback path) at head e2e09cb; kill tests run each interruption point in separate processes against a file-backed store; positive controls — the exit-probe test fails without process.exit, the flock test fails with flock disabled, the source scan fails on any new create-caller and on any allowed module losing its declaration. Independent review (spec §15, general-purpose reviewer with the opum-workflow specialist unavailable on a missing lore profile — WCLI-24): five rounds; it measured the pid-lock mutual-exclusion race (19 overlapping holder pairs in its stress) that prompted the flock redesign, re-measured zero pairs after it, and closed with nothing of substance standing. Stated limits: T01's status half is vacuous until a status command ships; the non-darwin fallback's check-then-delete race (unreachable today because the key provider refuses non-darwin) is recorded on WCLI-21 and WCLI-22 as a qualification precondition; a deleted vault with a surviving journal and key resumes the old identity (ADR 0001); a non-contention flock failure reports setup_in_progress (fail-closed).
